wavelength.short: The distance from one crest of a light wave to the next, written λ (lambda) and measured here in nanometres (nm). Visible light spans about 380 to 750 nm.

frequency.short: How many wave crests pass a point each second, written f and measured in hertz (Hz). For light, f = c/λ, so shorter wavelengths mean higher frequencies.

valence-band.short: The range of energies held by electrons that are tied up in the bonds between atoms. Electrons there cannot carry current on their own.

conduction-band.short: The range of energies at which an electron is free to wander through the crystal and carry current. It sits one band gap above the valence band.

thermalisation.short: The fast loss, as heat, of whatever energy a photon had above the band gap. The freed electron (and hole) shake the crystal lattice and settle to the band edge within about a trillionth of a second.

phonon.short: A packet of vibration of the crystal lattice: a quantum of heat and sound in a solid. Electrons shed excess energy by emitting phonons.

blackbody.short: An idealised object that absorbs all light and glows with a spectrum set only by its temperature. The Sun's light is close to that of a blackbody at about 5772 K.

detailed-balance.short: The principle that, in equilibrium, every process runs as often as its reverse. For a solar cell: a material that absorbs light well must also emit light, so some energy always leaks back out.

direct-band-gap.short: A band gap where an electron can jump from the top of the valence band to the bottom of the conduction band by absorbing a photon alone. Such materials (GaAs, CdTe, perovskites) absorb sunlight in a layer a few microns thick.

indirect-band-gap.short: A band gap where the jump also needs a kick of momentum from a lattice vibration (phonon). Absorption near the gap is weak, which is why silicon cells are made from wafers far thicker than thin-film cells.

absorption-coefficient.short: How quickly light of a given wavelength is absorbed as it travels into a material, per unit length. Its inverse is the absorption depth: the distance at which about 63 % of the light has been absorbed.

tandem-cell.short: A solar cell made of two or more stacked cells with different band gaps, so each band of colours is caught by the gap that wastes least of it.
